subject: FinTrust evaluation: security acceptance timeline, DPA redlines, and SIG clarifications
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>, FinTrust Procurement <procurement@fintrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed acceptance gates & timeline for FinTrust evaluation

Hi team —

Thanks again for the productive kickoff earlier. Per our MAP discussion, I wanted to put a concise security/compliance acceptance timeline on the record so we can align dependencies across procurement and legal. Attached is a one-page MAP CSV that maps each gate to owners and target dates (MAP_FT_timeline.csv).

High level:
- SIG/CAIQ: FinTrust to confirm critical control exceptions by 2027-05-20. We’ll provide the populated SIG matrix (FinTrust_SIG_v2.xlsx) and a short commentary on mitigations for items marked as "deferred."
- DPA: redline cycle — Redwood legal will produce a redline and expect back within 5 business days to avoid procurement delay. See DPA_redline_v3.docx attached.
- SOC 2 evidence review: we can provide the SOC 2 report and supporting artifact list by 2027-05-21; FinTrust security’s review window suggested is 10 business days.
- Data retention / deletion: propose default 90-day KV retention for evaluation workloads; pipeline for custom retention to be included in Dedicated/Private conversations.

Requests / asks for FinTrust:
1) Confirm whether SIG exceptions must be remediated prior to POC start or whether mitigations during POC are acceptable (answer needed by 5/20).
2) Assign a primary security point-of-contact for artifact intake (S3 share / secure upload).

Next steps: I’ll loop in Laura from Legal to confirm the DPA schedule and Neha for SOC 2 evidence packaging. Karthik will coordinate the SIG workbook changes.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Strategic Accounts 
Redwood Inference
(h) 415-555-0123

Attachment: MAP_FT_timeline.csv (3 rows)
Attachment: FinTrust_SIG_v2.xlsx (sheet: initial-populated)
Attachment: DPA_redline_v3.docx

From: Amy Jenkins <amy.jenkins@securesolutions.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed acceptance gates & timeline for FinTrust evaluation

Thanks, Hannah — useful baseline. A few clarifying Qs from the security review team: 

1) SIG scoping: can you confirm which model variants and data flows are represented in the SIG workbook? For POC we need explicit call/response examples and KV cache behavior documented (to assess transient data).

2) Data retention: 90-day KV retention is fine for logs, but the team needs a short note on encryption-at-rest key ownership for any persisted artifacts during the test — is Redwood-managed KMS being used or customer KMS in the Private deployment?

3) DPA: procurement is worried about clause 9.2 on subprocessor notifications. Can Redwood commit to 30 days notice for new subprocessors during the evaluation period?

We prefer short, bulleted responses so procurement can move the contract forward. I’ve attached a short checklist the FinTrust team uses for demos (Checklist_FT_demo.pdf) — will upload to your secure share later.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Jenkins <amy.jenkins@securesolutions.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed acceptance gates & timeline for FinTrust evaluation

Amy — quick responses inline and updates to the SIG workbook attached.

1) SIG scoping: The workbook covers the hosted API path (scheduled workloads) and the streaming chat path. KV cache behavior is documented on tab "KV_behavior" — short summary: ephemeral KV (per-session) is kept in GPU-local cache; persisted artifacts (for troubleshooting) are only stored if the customer explicitly enables log upload.

2) KMS model: For Hosted evaluation we use Redwood-managed KMS (AES-256, customer keys option is available on Private). I’ve added a note to the MAP timeline pointing to the Private deployment doc where customer KMS options and HSM integrations are listed.

3) Subprocessor notice: Redwood legal is OK with 30 days notice during an evaluation window; Laura will confirm the precise wording on the DPA redline.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: upload updated FinTrust_SIG_v3.xlsx with KV_behavior notes (done, see attachment).
- Neha: prepare SOC 2 evidence packet (artifact list + access instructions) by 2027-05-21.
- Laura: finalize DPA language on subprocessors and retention clause by 2027-05-18.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>, FinTrust Procurement <procurement@fintrust.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed acceptance gates & timeline for FinTrust evaluation

Hi all —

Quick legal note following Karthik's update. We updated the DPA_redline_v4.docx (attached) with the subprocessors clause changed to: "Redwood will provide written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to onboarding any new subprocessors that will process Customer Data during the evaluation period." If FinTrust needs a shorter notice window for production, we can discuss under Dedicated procurement terms.

On SOC 2 evidence: Neha will supply an artifact index and secure access (S3 pre-signed links) by 5/21. The SOC 2 report itself is available; we can provide the report under NDA if preferred.

On retention: we accepted the 90-day default for eval, with a process to request shorter retention in writing (email to support@redwood.ai). We also clarified deletion verification steps in the DPA redline (see section 4.3).

Please confirm procurement is comfortable with the 30-day subprocessor notice and that security has everything required to start the acceptance review.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_redline_v4.docx (redline vs v3)

From: FinTrust Security <security@fintrust.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTrust Procurement <procurement@fintrust.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed acceptance gates & timeline for FinTrust evaluation

Hannah / Laura / team —

Appreciate the rapid turnaround. We reviewed the updated SIG workbook and the DPA_redline_v4.docx. A few confirmations: 

- SIG: KV_behavior tab and the "ephemeral only unless enabled" language are sufficient for our POC acceptance. No further exceptions required to start.
- DPA: 30-day subprocessor notice acceptable for evaluation; procurement will accept DPA_redline_v4 for the POC period.
- SOC 2 evidence: we received the artifact index and the pre-signed links from Neha; we’ll begin the review Monday 5/24.
- Data retention: 90-day retention for evaluation confirmed. If we need faster deletion verification we will use the support process referenced in the DPA.

Next milestone: FinTrust security will provide a short acceptance note (1–2 paragraphs) after artifact review by 2027-06-04. Once we receive that acceptance the procurement team will move to signature and close the MAP.

Primary contact for security intake: security@fintrust.com

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

— FinTrust Security Team
